foods.name: Fresh Russet Potatoes (Homemade Fries / Wedges)
foods.description: High in free asparagine and reducing sugars. High-heat dry convection in air fryers rapidly triggers Maillard cascade on the outer dehydrated crust.
tips: Never store raw potatoes below 46°F (8°C); refrigeration triggers cold-induced sweetening, multiplying free sugars by up to 5x.
Soak cut potato batons in cold water for 25-30 minutes, or blanch in boiling water with a splash of vinegar for 3 minutes before air-frying.
Stop cooking when fries reach a uniform golden-yellow shade; avoid dark-brown or blackened tips.

foods.name: Frozen Par-Fried French Fries (Commercial)
foods.description: Commercially blanched and par-fried in industrial facilities, reducing surface sugars. However, high air-fryer temperatures can still produce elevated acrylamide if over-browned.
tips: Do not thaw before cooking; air-fry directly from frozen to avoid surface moisture accumulation and uneven scorching.
Shake the air fryer basket every 4-5 minutes to ensure uniform convective thermal distribution.
Follow package directions closely, and target 350°F (175°C) maximum rather than maximum 400°F setting.

foods.name: Sweet Potatoes (Fries / Cubes)
foods.description: Contains high natural sucrose and fructose concentrations. Surface caramelization and Maillard browning occur at lower temperatures than white potatoes.
tips: Because of elevated natural sugar content, sweet potatoes brown much faster; keep temperature at or below 340°F (170°C).
Lightly coat with high-smoke-point avocado or olive oil to buffer surface thermal transfer.
Check 3 minutes before standard cook recipes recommend to prevent scorching.

foods.name: Breaded Chicken Cutlets / Tenders
foods.description: Presents dual thermal hazard: the flour/breadcrumb crust generates acrylamide while high meat surface heat generates dietary AGEs and heterocyclic amines (HCAs).
tips: Ensure internal poultry core reaches verified safe 165°F (74°C) with an instant-read probe rather than judging by outer crust darkness.
Use panko breadcrumbs or crushed cornflakes without added corn syrup/sugar in the coating.
Marinate with rosemary or lemon juice beforehand; natural polyphenols reduce HCA and AGE formation by up to 60%.

foods.name: White Bread / Toast / Sourdough Croutons
foods.description: Wheat flour contains free asparagine while dough fermentation produces free glucose. Toasts with dark brown crust can exceed 250-400 ppb acrylamide.
tips: Aim for golden-yellow croutons; discard heavily browned or black charred pieces.
Sourdough fermentation breaks down free asparagine, resulting in 20-30% lower acrylamide than rapid-yeast white bread.
Air-fry at 300°F (150°C) for a gentle, even crisping without thermal scorching.

foods.name: Broccoli & Brussels Sprouts
foods.description: Cruciferous florets have very low asparagine, but thin outer leaves can char rapidly, forming bitter polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) if burned.
tips: Toss lightly with oil to prevent leaf tips from scorching into black carbonaceous ash.
Keep temperatures under 375°F (190°C) and check at the 10-minute mark.
Do not eat blackened, incinerated floret tips.

foods.name: Salmon Fillet & Fatty Fish
foods.description: Negligible acrylamide risk (virtually zero carbohydrate), but polyunsaturated omega-3 fatty acids oxidize readily into lipid hydroperoxides and dietary AGEs if overcooked.
tips: Cook to internal target temperature of 125°F - 130°F (52°C - 54°C) for tender medium-rare without albumin curdling.
Avoid high-temperature 400°F blistering which oxidizes delicate DHA and EPA fatty acids.
A light glaze of lemon or olive oil shields fish surface against circulating convective oxygen.

foods.name: Bacon Strips & Pork Belly
foods.description: Combines cured nitrates, animal proteins, and high lipid content. High convective heat catalyzes heterocyclic amines, volatile nitrosamines, and extreme dietary AGE levels (> 9,000 kU/100g).
tips: Air-fry at moderate temperature (340°F / 170°C) to render fat without smoking or charring meat fibers.
Ensure drippings fall into the catch pan beneath the basket so bacon does not bathe in smoking rendered fat.
Avoid uncured or candied bacon recipes containing brown sugar, which massively spike both acrylamide and AGEs.

preTreatments.name: None (Direct Cut to Air Fryer)
preTreatments.description: Raw unwashed pieces carry all surface starch and free sugars, allowing rapid early crust Maillard ignition.

preTreatments.name: Cold Water Soak (20 - 30 minutes)
preTreatments.description: Leaches out 40% - 45% of surface reducing sugars (glucose/fructose) and free asparagine before thermal exposure.

preTreatments.name: Par-Boil / Water Blanch (3 - 5 minutes)
preTreatments.description: Thermal water immersion gelatinizes outer starch and washes away up to 60% of Maillard precursors.

preTreatments.name: Acidic Water Pre-Dip (1 tbsp vinegar / 1L water)
preTreatments.description: Lowering surface pH below 5.5 protonates the free amino group of asparagine, blocking the initial nucleophilic addition reaction.

preTreatments.name: Stored in Refrigerator (< 46°F / 8°C) ⚠️
preTreatments.description: Cold-induced sweetening causes potato amylase enzymes to rapidly convert starch into free reducing sugars, supercharging acrylamide formation.

browningDonenessLevels.name: Light Blonde / Pale Yellow
browningDonenessLevels.description: Surface cooked through, light crisp, negligible caramelization.

browningDonenessLevels.name: Golden Yellow (Culinary Target)
browningDonenessLevels.description: Ideal crispness and flavor; complies with FDA & EFSA 'Go for Golden' guidance.

browningDonenessLevels.name: Deep Amber / Medium Brown
browningDonenessLevels.description: Advanced Maillard reaction; acrylamide accumulation rises substantially.

browningDonenessLevels.name: Dark Brown / Blackened Edges ⚠️
browningDonenessLevels.description: Thermal degradation, scorched protein/sugar crust, high AGEs and potential heterocyclic amine content.

toxicByproducts.name: Acrylamide (C₃H₅NO)
toxicByproducts.primaryTarget: Nerve terminals (peripheral neuropathy), reproductive & renal tissues

toxicByproducts.name: Advanced Glycation End-Products (dAGEs)
toxicByproducts.source: Non-enzymatic glycation of proteins/lipids during high dry heat
toxicByproducts.primaryTarget: Arterial stiffness, chronic renal dysfunction, oxidative stress
toxicByproducts.bmdl10: High dietary consumption linked to insulin resistance

toxicByproducts.name: Heterocyclic Aromatic Amines (HCAs)
toxicByproducts.source: Creatine/Creatinine + Amino Acids in meats cooked at > 375°F (190°C)

toxicByproducts.name: Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs)
toxicByproducts.source: Pyrolysis of fats dripping onto hot heating coils and rising in convection vapor
toxicByproducts.primaryTarget: Lung, gastrointestinal tract, systemic cellular DNA damage
toxicByproducts.bmdl10: Strict dietary minimization recommended by EFSA

mitigationGoldenRules.title: Go for Golden, Not Dark or Charred
mitigationGoldenRules.summary: Both FDA and EFSA urge consumers to aim for a light golden-yellow color when air-frying or baking potatoes and toast. Acrylamide concentrations increase exponentially once surface crust turns amber or dark brown.

mitigationGoldenRules.title: Cold Water Soak or 3-Minute Par-Boil
mitigationGoldenRules.summary: Submerging fresh cut potato pieces in water for 25-30 minutes washes away free surface starch and reducing sugars, cutting finished acrylamide levels by 40% to 50% without sacrificing crispness.

mitigationGoldenRules.title: Never Store Potatoes in the Refrigerator
mitigationGoldenRules.summary: Temperatures below 46°F (8°C) activate invertase enzymes in raw potatoes, breaking stored complex starches into free glucose and fructose. This 'cold-induced sweetening' can multiply acrylamide yield by 300% to 500%.

mitigationGoldenRules.title: Keep Air Fryer Temperature Below 360°F (180°C)
mitigationGoldenRules.summary: Because air fryers circulate concentrated superheated air with high convective velocity, foods reach surface dehydration much faster than in a conventional oven. Dropping temperature by 25°F and cooking 2-3 minutes longer preserves texture while drastically lowering thermal byproducts.

mitigationGoldenRules.title: Drain Rendered Fats Frequently
mitigationGoldenRules.summary: When cooking bacon, sausages, or fatty meats, ensure rendered grease drips through the perforated grate into the lower pan. Allowing fat to smoke or splatter back onto the top heating element vaporizes toxic PAHs.
